title: Converting integers between binary and decimal representation
recap: Each binary position has a power-of-two value. An unsigned binary value converts to decimal by adding the position values whose digits are one.
A decimal value can be converted one bit at a time with division and remainder. Signed integers use two's complement, so the same bit pattern can represent different values depending on its type.
objectives: Calculate each binary digit using integer division and remainder.
Format decimal values as grouped eight-bit output.
Reuse small functions instead of hard-coding binary strings.
warnings: This exercise intentionally avoids std::bitset and bitwise operations.
Integer division discards the remainder before % 2 selects the requested digit.
The unsigned and signed interpretations of a bit pattern are not interchangeable.
challenge: Implement printBit() and print8BitBinary() using only integer division and remainder. Print the decimal values 93 and 148 as grouped eight-bit binary values without std::bitset, bitwise operators, stdin, or hard-coded binary strings.
hints: Call printBit with 128, 64, 32, and 16, print a space, then use 8, 4, 2, and 1.
main should print each decimal label, call print8BitBinary, and then print a newline.
